To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brush border and the basal-lateral membranes are different with respect to their composition and function and that they are involved in different transport processes.

the brush border membrane contains a sodium-dependent glucose transport mechanism, a sodium-dependent amino-acid transport mechanism, and sodium-dependent transport mechanisms for galactose, phosphate, and sulfate, as well as sodium-independent transport mechanisms for galac-tose and sulfate.
the sodium-dependent glucose co-transport mechanism is a carrier-mediated transport system that can be inhibited by phlorizin and by phlorizin derivatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, characterization and regulation of transport mechanisms in the brush border and the basal-lateral membranes.
the elucidation of the biochemical mechanisms involved, on the one hand, in active transport of solutes across the intestinal and renal epithelium and, on the other, in the regulation of transport.
the elucidation of transport mechanisms in intestinal and renal epithelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the brush border membrane is involved in the active transport of sodium and chloride and in the passive exchange of hydrogen and chloride, whereas the basal-lateral membranes are involved in active calcium and inorganic-phosphate transport and in sodium/calcium counter-transport.

the brush border membrane is the site of sodium-coupled transport of glucose, amino acids, phosphate, and bicarbonate, while the basal-lateral membranes are the site of sodium-independent transport of glucose, sodium-dependent transport of calcium, and the site of a sodium/proton, and a chloride/hydroxyl exchange.

the brush border membrane is involved in sodium-dependent transport of glucose, amino acids, and other organic solutes as well as in sodium-dependent transport and exchange mechanisms of chloride and hydrogen ions, whereas the basal-lateral membranes are involved in transport mechanisms for sodium and calcium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to document the presence of different transport systems in the brush border and basal-latera membranes of intestine and proximal tubule, but we have not yet succeeded in defining their role in the intact cell and in the intact epithelium.
the transport systems of the intestinal and renal epithelia are complex and can be dissected into single components.
membrane vesicles are useful tools in the study of transport mechanisms in intestinal and renal proxymal tubular membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
membrane vesicle studies are a useful tool for studying membrane transport in the intestine and the kidney.
the brush border and basal-later membranes contain different transport mechanisms which are not identical with the transport systems present in the intact epithelial cell.
the study of membrane transport in membrane vesicles is an important and promising approach to obtain a deeper insight into the function of the renal and intestinal epithelium.
